newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour plans second-tier "stakeholder" pensions.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour plans second-tier "stakeholder" pensions.

text.p: The main opposition Labour party proposed on Wednesday a new form of collective second-tier funded pensions that it said would provide better value for money and hence more security than personal pensions.
Harriet Harman, the party's social security spokeswoman, said schemes that met high minimum standards would be approved by a Labour government as "Stakeholder Pensions."

Harman was due to give more details to a pensions conference in London on Wednesday. But she said in a statement previewing her speech that stakeholder pensions would offer improved benefits because their administrative costs would be much lower.
"Because they are a collective scheme -- multi-employer and multi-member -- they will have low overheads and offer individuals value for money," Harman said.

She said a Labour government would not increase the current level of compulsory employee contributions through National Insurance, but stakeholder pensions would attract additional voluntary contributions.

The party wants to encourage new partnerships to offer value-for-money pensions, involving local and national employers' organisations, trades unions and other employees' organisations, and financial services companies.
Labour calculates that a collective scheme could generate a pension as much as 35 percent higher than a personal pension for a worker on a modest annual income of 10,000 pounds a year.
